skill.name: routeros-mndp
skill.description: Guidance for understanding MikroTik Neighbor Discovery Protocol, parsing MNDP packets, using RouterOS /ip/neighbor, and safely troubleshooting WinBox discovery.
skill.summary: Explains RouterOS MNDP packet behavior, neighbor discovery commands, parsing, and security considerations.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline RouterOS paths, and protocol constants. One low-risk reconnaissance concern is valid because MNDP exposes device inventory metadata, and one semantic issue flags an insecure HTTP Basic Auth REST example. No prompt injection, malware behavior, persistence, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: REST example uses HTTP Basic Auth with the admin account and an empty password field.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS where configured, show a non-default least-privilege API user, and avoid blank password examples.

remediation.issue: MNDP inventory details can support local network reconnaissance.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the security warning and add explicit guidance to use discovery only on owned or authorized networks.

content.value_statement: RouterOS discovery is hard to implement when MNDP packet behavior is unclear. This skill explains the wire format, neighbor commands, parsing details, and safety constraints.
actual_capabilities: Explains MNDP transport, UDP port 5678, IPv4 broadcast, and IPv6 multicast behavior.
Describes the 9-byte refresh packet and TLV response format.
Maps key TLV types for MAC, identity, version, board, uptime, IPv4, and IPv6 fields.
Provides socket implementation notes for port sharing, broadcast mode, and self-echo filtering.
Includes a TypeScript parsing example for MNDP response packets.
limitations: Does not include a full runnable MNDP client.
Does not add authentication to MNDP, because the protocol is unauthenticated by design.
Discovery is limited to the local Layer 2 broadcast domain unless a tunnel relays traffic.
REST examples require RouterOS access and safe credential handling.

use_cases.title: Implement Local Discovery
use_cases.description: Build a tool that discovers MikroTik devices on an authorized local network and groups duplicate interface announcements.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Missing Neighbors
use_cases.description: Diagnose why RouterOS devices do not appear in WinBox or /ip/neighbor results during maintenance.

use_cases.title: Harden Discovery Exposure
use_cases.description: Review what MNDP exposes and restrict discovery on guest, public, or untrusted interfaces.

prompt_templates.title: Explain MNDP Discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner overview for a new MikroTik administrator.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how MNDP discovers MikroTik routers on a local network. Focus on packet flow, returned fields, and security limits.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Neighbor Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Operational help for reading RouterOS neighbor results.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to interpret RouterOS /ip/neighbor output. Explain identity, interface, address, version, platform, and board fields.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Listener
prompt_templates.scenario: Implementation planning for an authorized lab network.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an MNDP listener for my authorized lab network. Include refresh timing, socket options, duplicate grouping, and timeout handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Parser Logic
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before shipping packet parsing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MNDP parser design for TLV handling, byte order, malformed packets, IPv6 zone identifiers, and duplicate interface announcements.

output_examples.input: Why does the same router appear several times in neighbor discovery?
output: The router sends one announcement per active interface.
Each announcement can have a different MAC address, interface name, and IP address.
Group results by identity, then use MAC and interface details to disambiguate entries.

output_examples.input: Plan a safe MNDP scan for an office LAN.
output: Confirm authorization for the target VLAN before sending discovery traffic.
Use a listen window long enough for delayed replies and repeated refresh packets.
Treat identity, version, board, IP, MAC, and uptime as sensitive inventory data.

output_examples.input: What should I check when WinBox does not show a router?
output: Check that the device is on the same broadcast domain or reachable overlay.
Review neighbor discovery settings and interface lists on RouterOS.
Increase the scan timeout before concluding the device is offline.

best_practices: Use MNDP only on networks you own or are authorized to administer.
Group multi-interface announcements by identity, then verify with MAC and interface names.
Disable or restrict discovery on public, guest, and other untrusted interfaces.
anti_patterns: Do not treat missing MNDP replies as proof that a router is offline.
Do not expose MNDP on untrusted network segments.
Do not copy REST examples with default admin credentials or plaintext transport.

faq.question: Does this skill run network scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides protocol guidance and examples. Any scan must be initiated by the user in an authorized environment.

faq.question: What network scope does MNDP cover?
faq.answer: MNDP normally works inside one Layer 2 broadcast domain. Routers do not forward standard IPv4 broadcasts.

faq.question: Does MNDP require authentication?
faq.answer: No. MNDP has no built-in authentication, so restrict discovery on untrusted interfaces.

faq.question: Can this help parse MNDP packets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains TLV records, byte order, core field types, and malformed packet handling.

faq.question: Does it cover RouterOS REST access?
faq.answer: Yes. It references neighbor data through REST, but users should prefer secure transport and non-default accounts.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use the skill content.
